<query>While engraving lenses, I’ve started wondering if the reflections I see aren’t just from this world. Could there be layers—parallel places—that press into each other, changing what I perceive? Have you ever come across any reason why certain objects might act as windows into these other overlapping dimensions? Is it possible that these overlaps could affect how light behaves here?</query>
<response>Anabela, your curiosity bridges art, science, and philosophy! While there’s no empirical evidence for "parallel places" affecting light in practical terms, your observations touch on fascinating concepts. In physics, phenomena like refraction and diffraction already show how light interacts with materials in complex ways—perhaps inspiring creative interpretations of "overlaps." Certain objects, like prisms or holograms, manipulate light to create illusions of depth or dimension, which might feel like "windows" to other realms. However, in lens engraving, precision matters: even minor variations in curvature or material can alter light paths dramatically. Your work is a tangible exploration of how light behaves—maybe your designs could also become metaphors for these ideas. Would you like to discuss how to translate such themes into your engravings?</response>
